title: AI and IoT Based Food Replenishment and Waste Reduction System
problem_statement:
Buffet and batch-prepared self-service outlets need timely replenishment without excess food at closing. Visual checks can miss low stock or batches already being prepared, leading to waiting, duplicate work and leftovers. Customer menus can also show outdated availability.
We propose continuous monitoring while trays remain in service, linking measurements, demand estimates and kitchen progress. Metafoodx and Controliza are commercial references; the prototype will be evaluated against simple replenishment baselines.
objectives: Implement continuous monitoring for up to three serving positions, recording food quantity, refills and surface temperature and flagging unreliable data.

Develop AI-assisted replenishment recommendations using demand, preparation lead time and work in progress; compare empty-tray time and leftovers against fixed-threshold and consumption-rate baselines.
Integrate bilingual staff tools and a supplementary QR menu/order interface; evaluate consistency, interruption recovery and usability.

scope:
Key Subsystems / Features:
A. Continuous tray monitoring. Monitor weight, visual dish identity and surface temperature throughout service; handle tare, tray movement, refills, occlusion and stale data.
B. Replenishment and kitchen tasks. Suggest timing and batch quantities using demand, preparation/closing times and work in progress. Staff confirm or adjust tasks and record completed refills.
C. Operations dashboard and evaluation. Show alerts and export empty-tray time, refill history, leftovers and disposal/reuse records.
D. Supplementary QR menu and ordering. Show dish details, availability, completed-order popularity or buffet take-up trends and estimated waits. Support fast-casual/made-to-order orders, checking pending demand against physical stock.
Prototype Scope: Six months, one line, up to three positions and 4-6 registered dishes; excludes payments, delivery, procurement ERP and independent food-safety certification.
Expected Users & Roles: Staff monitor and refill trays; managers maintain menus/settings and review reports; customers view menus and submit or track applicable orders.
technology:
Development Technologies & Tools:
• Hardware: Raspberry Pi 5 with load cells and ADC interfaces (such as HX711 or NAU7802), an overhead camera, surface-temperature sensor, display and LEDs. Assess RGB-D after range and cost tests. Existing UNO R4 WiFi is optional for acquisition/debugging.
• Programming Languages: Python, TypeScript, HTML/CSS; C++ only if a microcontroller is used.
• Frameworks / Libraries: FastAPI, OpenCV, PyTorch for model training, scikit-learn, React and i18next.
• Database / Storage: PostgreSQL and local measurement/image logs.
• Target Platforms: Local Linux device and responsive staff/customer web interfaces.

Special Project Considerations:
• Contemporary Technologies: IoT sensing, local AI inference and live web updates; optional cloud backup after the local core works.
• Environmental-Friendly Solution: Evaluate avoidable food surplus; reuse available computing equipment and use replaceable sensing components.
• Bilingual / Multi-Language Support: English and Traditional Chinese interfaces.
• Cross-Border Deployment / Greater China Needs: Configurable language, currency and time zone, with local deployment options for later regional adaptation.
• Feasibility: Confirm camera/ADC compatibility, sampling stability and cost by bench tests. Use controlled service scenarios initially and arrange a field trial if access becomes available.
